decisions.summary: a tree is a circle with the canopy fill (TREE_FILL #7A8C5C), own or its group's, or in <g id="trees">; the fence group's lines become fence_segs
decisions.why: FR-001 word for word - a tree is known by its drawing so the sheets drawn before this feature carry trees without a retrofit; the fill is the one every pool sheet's canopies already carry (verified: the shrine sheet and the four magistracy sheets). fence_segs is what FR-002's 'a wall or fence stroke' needs.

decisions.summary: shared.trees_overlap: a canopy against every footprint, furniture rect, wall band, divider, fence segment, non-tree glyph, tub and label by closest-point distance and against every other canopy, tolerance WALL_OVERLAP_MIN_PX; fixture = the Hoshigaoka sheet as committed
decisions.why: the list matches FR-002's list; the tolerance is the built-footprint overlap check's own constant (checks.py WALL_OVERLAP_MIN_PX = 0.5, used by shared.py's footprint overlap), which is what FR-002 demanded instead of a second number. FR-002 itself names the committed sheet as the artifact the check must fire on, so using it as the red fixture serves both clauses; US1's building-corner case is owed by T03's unit tests, not by the fixture.

decisions.summary: the declaration line and its parser: **On map**: <manifest> - <key> at (x, y) = <sheet id>, Context.on_map
decisions.why: FR-003's line, with one field added: the trailing '= <sheet id>' names the rect that IS the subject, which FR-004(a)'s transform needs an origin for and which FR-003's own shape does not supply. It adds information rather than removing any, and FR-003's named parts are all present. RECORD-KEEPING: FR-003 quotes the line literally and should be amended to carry the field, so spec, contracts/on-map.md and onmap.py agree.

decisions.summary: mapmatch.py: load_map, the CLASSES table, the Transform, frame_in_map, and check(ctx) running directions (b), (c), (d) with MAP_GRAIN_PX = 15
decisions.why: the class table reproduces FR-004's table row for row, the water point (well or basin) as one class included; the grain is m:map-grain (R1), whose command re-runs and reproduces the ring radii 54/66/80/96/112 and the torii pitch of 15 px; the declaration refusals are FR-005's.

decisions.summary: two registry rows, both shared, each with a red fixture; the report prints both in registry order
decisions.why: FR-002, FR-004 and FR-008 as written.

decisions.summary: site items: a required program item gains "site": "<class>" and is asked for only where the declared map shows that class inside the frame; the shrine's grove (tree) and burial_ground are the two; with no declaration the item is required as before
decisions.why: this is the GM's own sentence - 'we shouldn't put any trees or graveyard on the shrine diagram if those are not in correspnding places on the village map' - and both classes it covers are classes the GM named, so the one justification is not stretched over two unlike things. FR-006 requires no grove and no burial ground on the redrawn sheet and FR-007 requires the shrine program's site knob to say so; a program item left unconditional would have made FR-006 fail check_program. The no-declaration path keeps every other sheet's program whole.

decisions.summary: the redraw per R3: hall 60 x 48 ft facing south, arch 20 ft in front, well 108 ft north on the axis inside a fence carried north, swept ground to the frame, no grove, no burial ground, no lane outside the arch; the frame and the overrides in the notes
decisions.why: every figure is FR-006's or R3's, including the frame (60 ft in front of the arch, 20 ft behind the well, 100 ft either side). Dropping the lane outside the arch is not in FR-006's list but follows from FR-004(b): the map records no lane there, so a sheet lane would be a feature the map does not show.

decisions.summary: the rule written into buildings.md, the shrine program's knob 4, and a building-review pass
size-audit and building-review on the redrawn sheet, one agent each, two ledger rows, escalation-check
unit tests per module, the registry test, the sweep, make done at 100%, m:sweep-cost re-measured
the crop check yields to a declared map: viewbox_cropped does not run on a sheet with an **On map** line, and the report says why (frame_is_the_maps)
decisions.why: It IS an except-when against a registered check, and FR-006 says the redrawn sheet 'passes every registered check', so it was judged as an exception rather than waved through. It survives all three tests. (1) Impossible otherwise: FR-006 fixes the frame in feet - 100 ft either side of the axis, 60 ft in front of the arch, 20 ft behind the well - precisely so the lane, grove, pond and byre stay outside it (R3), while viewbox_cropped requires no side to leave more than ~25 px of parchment beyond the INK, and ink_bounds discounts a page-filling ground rect (its 'nothing drawn to crop to' path), so the swept ground cannot supply the ink. The two rules cannot both hold without changing FR-006's stated numbers. (2) Implied by the GM's words: 'make the diagram view match what is shown on the larger map' makes the map, not the ink, the chooser of the view; the crop rule's premise is the opposite one and is what the request inverts. (3) It does not gut the rule's purpose: an oversized frame is still bounded, by FR-004(c), which requires every map feature inside the frame to be on the sheet, and the two non-margin findings are not lost - mapmatch reports 'the sheet has no viewBox, so its frame cannot be laid on the map'. RECORD-KEEPING: the exception lives only in plan.md and registry.py; FR-006's 'passes every registered check' should carry the clause.

decisions.summary: a size is held to one map px per side, a position to the 15 px grain
decisions.why: FR-004(d) as amended states exactly this, with the same reason (the map records a footprint to the pixel and a sheet can draw it exactly; the grain is for positions the map placed by search), and R1's decision paragraph says it too. The plan restates the spec rather than deciding anything.

decisions.summary: unlabeled: T04 fixes Ubame's garden trees if the new shared check fires on that sheet
decisions.why: SC-001 requires every live Mode A sheet to pass the check after the redraw, and FR-002 makes the check shared, not the shrine's.

decisions.summary: unlabeled: the research record's country-shrine pages are not touched; the override is recorded in buildings.md, the sheet's notes and the spec
decisions.why: the spec's Decisions Recorded table places the record in exactly those places and says the record's country-shrine section is unchanged; the map overrides this SHEET, not the research.
